main_body: Cottage: a large terracotta tile roof slope over a cream plaster and timber front wall, with an arched wooden door in a stone frame, a shuttered window, a lantern and a stone plinth.
top_band: At x=32 the roof slope runs from rows 3 to 41. It is light salmon (L=175/145) at the top rows 4-12 and darkens to L=61-52 at rows 29-41 near the eave. A chimney top sits at rows 0-12 on the right.
evidence: The roof is a big tile slope seen from above, with a light-to-dark gradient and per-tile scallops, not a thin cap line. It ends in a dark eave row at rows 40-41 (L=33-47) that shades the wall below. The south wall is a separate vertical face with timber framing. The door sits inside a stone frame and the window has a dark inner top, shutters and a sill, so both read as inset. The roof slope is the visible horizontal surface, as in the Beodeul references. There is no receding side face. The roof is a front-facing gable slope rather than a hip, but it still reads as a top surface above a front face.

style.evidence: The roof has about six tile tones (L 175, 145, 115, 89, 65, 47) with per-tile highlights and dark seams. The plaster is speckled, and the door has plank grain and iron bands. The outline is tinted dark red-brown beside the roof and brown beside the timber, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral. Flat-fill coverage is 2%, comparable to the references. At 10 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 42 distinct colours against 66 and 185, it is a little lower than the references but not shallow. It would sit acceptably next to house-h112 (stone).
